questions.question: When checking your tires before riding, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes the alcohol.
The less the alcohol will affect you.
The more likely you will avoid getting pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober, though they may help you stay awake.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and let them get in front of you. Riding faster may make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that are at an angle to your lane, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to ride on the shoulder to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight through your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could drift into another lane.

questions.question: In a crash, you have a better chance of avoiding serious injury if you do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Reduce your injury risk by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: It is easier to judge distances than during the day.
Using high beam headlights always makes it hard to see.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no oncoming traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: When choosing where to position your motorcycle in a lane, what should you think about?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead of you.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
Whether you can pass more vehicles from that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has many advantages. Most importantly, make sure other drivers can see you and that you have enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider constantly watch for on the road ahead?
questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead for changing traffic, hazards, and places you could go to avoid danger. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot for other vehicles.
Trust your mirrors to see everything around you.
Point in the direction you plan to go.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is also called engine braking.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: No jacket if the weather is warm.
A jacket at all times, even in warm weather.
You don't need to worry about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: A jacket at all times, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of good material when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket helps protect you and prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants too, and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to pressure them not to ride.

questions.question: How can you reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: Wearing a good-quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is the most important piece of safety equipment for a motorcycle rider.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Turn it on only when it's cloudy.
Turn it on if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: How do you make the shortest and safest stops?

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both brakes smoothly and gradually, without letting either tire skid.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Choose a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. When you downshift, your brake lights do not turn on.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has survived a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the most protection. A good helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how your motorcycle works, how to operate it, and when to maintain it.

questions.question: How can you help drivers merge into your lane from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move into the next lane if you can.
Do nothing, since they are merging, not you.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Move to a different lane if you can to give them plenty of space to merge safely.

questions.question: Which feature is NOT required on a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Which color makes you easier to see while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible while riding. Use bright colors any time you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should you wear when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang loose.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they do not catch on anything. Laces should be tucked in so they cannot get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them?
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoelaces in securely so they cannot catch on any part of your motorcycle.

questions.question: How should riders be positioned when entering a curve in a group?

options.text: In rows of three across the lane.

questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation, but switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway for safety.
